name: Tamarindo
hero_description: Costa Rica's buzzing Pacific surf town on the Nicoya Peninsula.
description: Tamarindo is Guanacaste's largest developed beach town, transformed from a small fishing village into a lively surf and eco-tourism hub. Popular with surfers, digital nomads, and expats, it blends renowned surf breaks with a vibrant arts and nightlife scene.
why_visit: Once a sleepy fishing village, Tamarindo boomed in the 21st century thanks to surfing and eco-tourism, famously boosted by its appearance in the 1994 film The Endless Summer II. Today it's the largest developed beach town in Guanacaste and the most accessible spot along Costa Rica's northern Pacific coast.

Beyond the waves, the area offers excellent sport fishing, scuba diving at the Catalina Islands, several nearby golf courses, and access to Las Baulas National Marine Park, an important nesting site for endangered leatherback sea turtles. A night market, food truck park, fire performances, and electronic music festivals round out a lively town scene.
highlights: Surf breaks suitable for beginners through advanced riders
Excellent sport fishing with numerous charter captains
Scuba diving at the nearby Catalina Islands
Leatherback turtle nesting at adjacent Las Baulas National Marine Park
Vibrant culture with night market, food trucks, and music festivals
Nearby golf courses including Hacienda Pinilla and Reserva Conchal
considerations: Tamarindo has faced water-quality issues, losing and regaining its Blue Flag beach designation over the years; it reportedly regained it in 2018.
As Guanacaste's largest developed beach town and a festival destination, it can feel busy and commercialized compared to quieter villages.
The drive from San Jose takes 3.5 to 6 hours depending on traffic, though Liberia International Airport is only about an hour away.

faq.a: Yes. Tamarindo and nearby areas are very popular for surfing, with waves ranging from beginner to advanced level.

faq.q: How do I get to Tamarindo?
faq.a: The closest international airport is Liberia International Airport, about an hour away. There is also a local airstrip and daily bus service to and from San Jose.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Tamarindo?
faq.a: Tamarindo has two seasons: a dry season from December to April and a wet season generally from May to November.
